reuse.why: It makes the existing shared getScheduledAmount the single expected-amount rule (reusing getApproxNumberThreshold) and routes the server, forecast, template, preview and API paths through it.

duplication.why: Five inline midpoint/missing-amount copies are deleted in favour of the shared helper and no new copies are introduced.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts, used by both server and client, and the API field is added in the api handler with a typed list entity.

scope.why: Focused on the expected-amount rule and the API field; the UI call sites now pass op too, which is needed for consistency, though useScheduleEdit's second call is left unchanged.

maintainability.why: One documented function with an op parameter and thorough unit tests now decides the expected amount everywhere.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gained an op parameter (inserted before inverse, all callers updated); the approximate branch is the rule itself, and all former inline copies now call the helper
